input: Compile a list of emergency home repair contacts

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The types of emergencies covered (plumbing, electrical, structural, HVAC, etc.) directly determine which trade categories and specialists need to be included in the list.
The geographic location determines which local contractors, utility providers, and municipal services are actually reachable and relevant.
Whether the list is for a single household, a landlord managing multiple properties, or a property manager changes the scale and structure of the list.
A budget constraint (e.g., preference for free/low-cost services, insurance-covered contractors) affects which contacts are prioritised or vetted.
The intended format (printed sheet, phone contacts, shared document, app) shapes how the list is structured and what information fields are needed per entry.
Knowing what 'done well' looks like — e.g., verified contacts with 24/7 availability vs. a quick rough list — determines the depth of research required.
Whether the user prefers nationally recognised chains, local independent tradespeople, or contacts already vetted by neighbours/reviews affects sourcing strategy.

gold.taskTitle: Compile emergency home repair contacts list
gold.taskDescription: Build a organised list of contacts to call when urgent home repair situations arise.

questions.title: Which repair types must the list cover?
questions.description: Identify the specific emergency categories to include — such as plumbing, electrical, gas, roofing, HVAC, pest, or locksmith — so no critical trade is missed.

questions.title: What city or region is this list for?
questions.description: Pinpoint the geographic location so that only locally available contractors, utility emergency lines, and municipal services are researched and included.

questions.title: Who will be using this contacts list?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is for a single homeowner, a renter, a landlord with multiple units, or a property management team, as this affects the scale and ownership structure.

questions.title: Should contacts be limited to insurance-approved providers?
questions.description: Determine whether budget or insurance constraints mean the list should prioritise contractors covered by a home warranty or insurance policy over general-market options.

questions.title: What format should the finished list take?
questions.description: Decide whether the output should be a printed reference sheet, a saved contacts group on a phone, a shared digital document, or another format for quick access during an emergency.

questions.title: Should every contact have confirmed 24/7 availability?
questions.description: Establish the quality bar — whether each entry must be verified for round-the-clock emergency response, or whether a faster, less rigorously vetted list is acceptable.

questions.title: Do you prefer local independents or national service chains?
questions.description: Understand the sourcing preference — locally recommended tradespeople, nationally recognised brands with guarantees, or a mix — to guide where contacts are found.
